🔥🇲🇽 <u>One-year ban for the SRE official who held his wedding at MUNAL</u>

Mexico's Anti-Corruption and Good Government Ministry barred Martín Borrego Llorente, Alicia Bárcena's former chief of staff at the SRE, from public office for one year. He requested the National Art Museum's reception hall for what he billed as an official event. It was his wedding. Borrego, who resigned from Semarnat when the case broke, insists it was a diplomatic event paid for privately. His sanction is one of a package covering 82 public servants, one private individual and one company.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>UIF freezes accounts of Córdova-era INE director</u>

Mexico's Financial Intelligence Unit (UIF) added Juan Carlos Cuervo Escalona, the INE's director of coordination and analysis under Lorenzo Córdova, to its List of Blocked Persons over suspected illicit operations tied to electoral contracts. La Jornada links him to the Hernández Casillas brothers, the contractors at the center of the INE procurement scandal. Cuervo left the INE in 2023 and that same year became legal representative of Corporativo ZEG. The red flags: simulated bidding and alleged misuse of public money.

🇲🇽🛒 <u>Onions up 82%, tomatoes up 44%: Mexico's food basket outpaces inflation</u>

INEGI's October poverty-line report shows the urban food basket rose 5.9% year on year and the rural one 5.6%, both above 3.8% headline inflation. Onions (+82.2%), tomatoes (+43.9%) and eating out drove the increase. A city dweller now needs 2,594.39 pesos a month for basic food and 4,985.47 pesos to cover all basic needs (+4.7%). The 2026 minimum wage of 315.04 pesos a day still covers that full line almost twice over, and the 2027 wage talks are underway right now, reports El Economista.

🇲🇽📊 <u>INEGI: deaths in Mexico fell 3.4% in 2025</u>

INEGI recorded 792,187 deaths in Mexico in 2025, down 27,485 from the 819,672 registered in 2024. The national crude rate was 606 per 100,000 people. Of the total, 89.9% came from illness and 10.1% from external causes (accidents, homicides and suicides). The top killers remain chronic: heart disease, diabetes, malignant tumors, liver disease, then accidents.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Under Taddei, the INE handed out 96% of its contracts without bidding</u>

A La Jornada review found that Mexico's electoral institute awarded 96% of more than 13,300 service, lease and procurement contracts by direct assignment during Guadalupe Taddei's tenure, worth over 2.829 billion pesos. One firm, Jurídicos Integrales FBP, got at least 96 contracts totaling 54.13 million pesos. The largest award went to AMPS, the company that installed the surveillance cameras with microphones in the INE's press room and offices. Taddei resigned as INE president on Oct. 26.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>From Beijing to the IMF board: Sheinbaum puts Jesús Seade on the Fund's executive directorate</u>

Speaking from Shenzhen at the APEC summit, President Sheinbaum announced that Jesús Seade, Mexico's ambassador to China since 2021, will leave the embassy to join the IMF's executive board, where he'll represent Mexico and eight other countries. "Lo propuse y fue aceptado," she said. Seade negotiated the T-MEC for Mexico as undersecretary for North America, and the move comes a day after the IMF itself rejected Washington's claim that Mexico is a "trampoline" for Chinese goods. Sheinbaum also has a meeting with IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva on her agenda in China; Georgieva asked for it.

🇲🇽🚢 <u>Progreso port triples in size as Plan México reaches the southeast</u>

The expansion of Yucatán's deep-water port at Progreso is a three-stage program worth over 12.5 billion pesos, El Financiero reports. Stage one, funded by the state with 1.63 billion pesos, finished in June: the navigation channel now runs 8.1 km, is 180 meters wide and 13.30 meters deep, up from 11.75. Stage two, 948 million pesos from SSA Marine, enlarges the cruise terminal. Carnival has announced 50 calls for 2028, and the port aims to go from about 400,000 cruise passengers a year toward one million. Stage three, run by the Navy, takes the port from 34 to 114 hectares. Concamin's president said Yucatán's progress "exceeded expectations" and announced a permanent working group with the state.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>Mexico's Supreme Court upholds prison for medical negligence</u>

By majority vote, the SCJN declared constitutional articles 60 and 291 of the Federal Penal Code, which punish medical staff who cause permanent harm to patients through lack of professional care. The case: an IMSS surgeon who operated twice on a patient's spine in December 2017, leaving him with permanently reduced mobility in his right leg. The Court, on a draft by Justice María Estela Ríos, drew the line clearly: complications and the inherent risks of medicine are not crimes. Criminal liability applies only when a doctor breached a concrete duty of care and that omission caused the harm.

🇲🇽🇨🇳 <u>Mexico looks to China to turn garbage into electricity</u>

On the way to the APEC summit in Shenzhen, Environment Secretary Alicia Bárcena toured China's waste-to-energy plants on President Sheinbaum's instructions. The SUS Environment plant in Zhuhai processes 3,000 tons of waste a day and generates up to 90 megawatts; Shenzhen's Nanshan eco-energy park treats 2,300 tons a day. Semarnat wants technology cooperation to turn organic waste, sargassum included, into power and cut emissions. Bárcena noted that China went from recovering energy from 9.8% of its urban waste in 2005 to 84.6% in 2024.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>The IMF answers Washington: Mexico is not a "trampoline" for Chinese goods</u>

A day after US Ambassador Ronald Johnson accused China of "flooding" Mexico with cheap imports, the IMF's annual report on Mexico undercuts the triangulation story. Using OECD input-output tables for 2010-2022, the Fund finds that about half of the rise in Mexico's imports from China comes from Mexican domestic demand, nearly a third from China's overall export growth, and the rest from intermediate goods that go into Mexico's own exports. In August, Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard said Mexico has not identified transshipment above 1% of its foreign trade.
banner: IMF: MEXICO IS NO CHINA TRAMPOLINE
